one_liner: META surged 6.6% on Sep 9 on AI product/chip news but score of 33/100 reflects broken EMA structure and weak RS — wait for the dust to settle.

price_action.intraday_story: META closed up 0.49% in a quiet session following the explosive 6.55% surge on Sep 9. The two-day consolidation after a gap-up is telling — buyers absorbed the move cleanly but volume faded. Stock needs to hold $640 to validate the Sep 9 move as a pivot rather than a trap.

news_catalyst.headline: JPMorgan upgrades META after Iris AI chip reveal and paid AI agent launch
news_catalyst.summary: Three simultaneous catalysts drove the 6.6% surge: (1) JPMorgan upgrade following AI product announcements, (2) in-house Iris AI chip entering production in September 2026 (Broadcom-designed, TSMC-fabricated), and (3) launch of a paid personal AI agent — Meta's first consumer AI monetisation. Separately, META agreed to an $18B settlement with limits on younger users, a known overhang now cleared. The Iris chip reduces dependency on NVIDIA and signals long-term margin expansion. The AI agent monetisation is nascent but strategically significant.

technical.summary:
META's EMA structure is weaker than NVDA's, explaining the lower Trend Health score (8/30). EMA-50 is not significantly above EMA-200, and the RS rating of 43 indicates the stock has been lagging SPY over the past 12 weeks. The Sep 9 gap-up is a positive development but one candle doesn't fix a 3-month relative underperformance pattern.

The stock is testing resistance around $650-670. A sustained hold above $650 with volume confirmation would be the first sign that the trend is genuinely turning. Until EMA-50 begins rising consistently and RS improves above 60, this remains a 'news-driven pop in a structurally weak trend' scenario.

No VCP or Wyckoff signal detected. The $18B settlement clearing is a net positive for removing an overhang, but the technical picture needs more time to recover.

wyckoff_narrative: META shows no tagged Wyckoff events in the 90-day dataset. The stock appears to be in a late Accumulation or early Markup phase following what may have been a distribution-and-reset cycle in 2026. The Sep 9 surge on significant news could be interpreted as a Sign of Strength if confirmed by: (1) a secondary test of $630-640 on declining volume, followed by (2) a higher high above $670. Without confirmation, the single-day move is ambiguous — it could be a Spring or simply a news-driven bounce within a range.

valuation.summary: META's DCF shows ~11% upside to base case $720, which is below the 15% threshold for a strong DCF signal. The Iris chip and AI agent monetisation aren't yet in the model's growth assumptions. If those materialise, the bull case strengthens meaningfully. At current price, the stock is fairly valued to slightly undervalued — not a compelling DCF buy but not expensive either.

key_concerns: $18B legal settlement is a one-time but significant hit
fundamentals.summary: META scores B (0.72) — solid but not elite. The settlement removes a known risk. In-house AI chips are strategically positive but 2-3 year payoff horizon. Fundamentals support holding a position but don't compel new entry at current levels without technical confirmation.
